tip.title: Alike and different
tip.text: To COMPARE is to find what is alike. To CONTRAST is to find what is different. Signal words for alike: both, also, similarly, like. Signal words for different: but, however, unlike, while, on the other hand. A quick way to organize: make two columns and list the same features side by side (cost, time, safety) so you compare the same thing for each.

passage.title: Two Ways to School
passage.text:
Twins Marco and Mina live in the same house and go to the same school, but they get there in very different ways.

Marco rides a jeepney. It costs twelve pesos each way and takes about twenty minutes when the road is clear. However, the jeepney stops often to pick up passengers, and during the rainy season traffic can double the travel time. On those mornings, Marco says, the jeepney crawls like a tired snail. Marco likes it because he can sit, review his notes, and arrive without sweating.

Mina walks. The route along the river path takes thirty minutes, rain or shine. It costs nothing, and she says the morning air helps her wake up. On the other hand, she arrives tired on hot days, and when the path floods she has to take the long road around, adding fifteen minutes.

Both twins leave home at six-thirty. Both usually arrive before the first bell. Their mother says the two routes suit the two children: Marco, who likes comfort and planning, and Mina, who likes being outdoors and saving her allowance for books.

words.meaning: the way or path you take to get somewhere
words.example: The bus takes a different route on Sundays.

words.meaning: people riding in a vehicle who are not driving it
words.example: The jeepney was full of passengers.

words.meaning: to be right or good for someone

items.prompt: Which sentence from the text BEST supports the idea that the jeepney is not always fast?
choices: Marco rides a jeepney.
It costs twelve pesos each way.
However, the jeepney stops often to pick up passengers, and during the rainy season traffic can double the travel time.
Marco likes it because he can sit.
items.why: Stopping often and traffic that "can double the travel time" are the proof that the ride can be slow. The other lines are about cost or comfort.

items.prompt: How is Mina's route DIFFERENT from Marco's?
choices: It costs nothing and takes longer.
It is faster and more expensive.
It has more passengers.
It lets her review her notes.
items.why: Walking is free and takes thirty minutes; the jeepney costs twelve pesos and takes about twenty.

items.prompt: Which signal word in the passage introduces a CONTRAST?
choices: Both
Also
However
Same
items.why: "However, the jeepney stops often" shows a difference from the quick twenty-minute trip.

items.prompt: Which sentence BEST supports the idea that walking has a downside for Mina?
choices: Mina walks.
It costs nothing, and she says the morning air helps her wake up.
On the other hand, she arrives tired on hot days.
Both usually arrive before the first bell.
items.why: Arriving tired is the bad side of walking. The other lines are neutral or show the good side.

items.prompt: What problem do BOTH routes share?
choices: They cost too much.
Rain can make the trip longer.
The twins arrive late every day.
The school is far away.
items.why: Traffic doubles in the rainy season for Marco; the flooded path adds fifteen minutes for Mina.

items.prompt: What is one way Marco's and Mina's trips are ALIKE?
choices: Both cost twelve pesos.
Both leave home at six-thirty.
Both take exactly twenty minutes.
Both walk along the river.
items.why: "Both twins leave home at six-thirty." The other choices describe only one twin.

items.prompt: Which sentence BEST supports the idea that neither twin is usually late for school?
choices: Both usually arrive before the first bell.
They get there in very different ways.
The route along the river path takes thirty minutes, rain or shine.
Their mother says the two routes suit the two children.
items.why: Arriving "before the first bell" is the proof that they are on time. The other lines are about the routes, not about being late or early.

items.prompt: "The jeepney crawls like a tired snail." What does this comparison mean?
choices: The jeepney is very small.
The jeepney moves very slowly in the rain.
The jeepney is old and dirty.
The jeepney carries animals.
items.why: A snail is known for moving slowly. The simile paints the rainy-day jeepney as slow, which matches "traffic can double the travel time."

items.prompt: Mina's walk takes thirty minutes "rain or shine." What does this idiom mean?
choices: Only on sunny days
Only on rainy days
No matter what the weather is
When the rain stops and the sun comes out
items.why: "Rain or shine" is an expression meaning in any weather. The sentence says her walk takes the same time whatever the weather.

items.prompt: "On the other hand, she arrives tired on hot days." What does the expression on the other hand mean here?
choices: She carries her bag in her other hand.
Looking at the opposite side of the matter
She waves at people on the path.
Her hands get tired from walking.
items.why: The expression is not about real hands. It introduces the opposite side: the good points of walking came first, and now the bad point.
